items.text: Scratchpad smoke tests may call _queue_dev_scratchpad_command directly after sourcing queuebash.sh. This is intentional for focused ledger testing because public queue dev scratchpad goes through _queue_init and bundled installer walking. Public dispatch is covered statically in this package.
Do not integrate queue dev test with scratchpad in 0.18.24. The integration target remains a later package where queuebash.dev_test_result.v1 evidence can be attached to scratchpad tasks.
Do not add prompt rendering to the scratchpad import contract package. Prompt rendering belongs in a later package after next --json and export --json are stable.
Architect delivery requirement: add queue dev scratchpad list and queue dev scratchpad delete ITEM_ID to improve day-to-day scratchpad usability after 0.18.24 acceptance.

Remote dev runner landmine: a generic HTTP command runner is remote code execution. v1 must expose only named, capability-scoped operations and must reject arbitrary command strings, shell metacharacter execution, environment injection, and unapproved file targets.

Remote dev runner must default to binding on 127.0.0.1 for SSH-tunnel use. Public bind must require an explicit option, print a warning, and still require session id, auth code, TTL, and workspace confinement.

Remote dev runner must never store or echo auth tokens, SSH private keys, OCI config, API keys, PAR URLs, or uploaded secrets into scratchpad, package zips, repository files, or normal logs. Returned logs must be bounded and should redact obvious secret-bearing fields.

Remote dev runner package must not alter queue dev test, queue dev scratchpad, job-resolution behaviour, governance provider contracts, or OCI provider contracts except for documentation references. It is a new dev infrastructure bridge only.

Future remote service plugin must be auth-gated and policy-gated. It may expose selected queue commands and dev functions only through named operations, with session/auth checks, bounded execution, scoped process control, and audit logging. It must not become a generic remote shell.

Remote service landmine: once this evolves beyond dev runner, every exposed operation must be treated as a security boundary. Authentication alone is not enough; commands must also be policy-gated, allowlisted, audited, bounded, and scoped to the remote service session or queue context.

OCI work must preserve cloud legal/compliance concerns: sovereignty and region mapping, retention/deletion policy, auditability, shared-responsibility explanation, sensitive PAR/credential redaction, cross-border review flags, and primary-source validation before accepting legal claims.

items.text: Remote queue service provider work and cloud resource provider work are separate packages. Remote service may expose authorized queue/dev operations on a remote machine. Cloud resource provider tracks and claims capacity/resources. Neither package should absorb the other.

Cloud infrastructure helpers and cloud resource provider remain separate layers. Helpers can start/stop/status named services when explicitly gated. The resource provider records inventory, claims, provenance and policy-consumable facts. Neither layer may become queue dispatch logic.

items.text: queue ask landmine: advisory output for customer databases or cross-border deployments must not imply that setting sovereign:region_in alone is sufficient. It should distinguish technical region gating from legal authority, data-transfer basis, retention/legal hold, customer-data classification, audit evidence, and local policy configuration.

Azure backfill is not first-tier parity yet. Do not claim Azure equality from provider-pack files alone; first-tier requires validated identity, region/sovereignty, legal/compliance, FinOps/cost, resource, fixtures, explainability and tests.

EU sovereign cloud provider work remains mapped/pending validation. Do not claim legal compliance, sovereign status, or first-tier parity until provider-specific primary-source validation, legal review, fixtures, JSON contracts, explainability, and tests support it.
APAC/China provider contracts remain mapped pending primary-source validation. Do not claim compliance, first-tier parity, or legal suitability from Alibaba/Tencent/Huawei fixture packs alone.

GPU cloud provider work must remain contract-first and fail-closed. It must not store API keys, kubeconfigs, model registry secrets, signed URLs, SSH private keys, or bearer tokens in job files or normal logs.

GPU cloud landmine: GPU capacity is not just instance count. Accelerator family, quota, reservation/availability, driver/CUDA stack, data residency, export-control posture, model/artifact handling, and cost ceilings may independently block a claim.

Cloud provisioning split: cloud_resource owns inventory, claims, releases, heartbeat, reconcile, provenance, and policy-consumable facts. cloud_infra owns gated lifecycle start/stop/status helpers. cloud_provision owns named templates, plan/validate/explain workflow, policy gates, dry-run evidence, and future registry handoff.

Provisioning landmine: do not let cloud provisioning become scheduler logic. Queue dispatch may consume cloud_resource availability and claim facts through assets/classes, but must not directly call cloud provider lifecycle operations or create servers during ordinary submit/dispatch.

Shared rule for all Bobs: fixture-first by default. New provider/platform work must not require live credentials, live API calls, provisioning/destruction, or cloud mutation for default tests. Live behaviour must be explicitly gated, audited, bounded, and deferred unless the package scope says otherwise.

Shared rule for all Bobs: do not refactor queuebash.sh dispatch, job state transitions, or worker execution semantics unless explicitly tasked. Prefer additive docs, providers.d helpers, policies.d examples, assets/classes where cleanly supported, fixtures, JSON contracts, and tests.

Bob2 provider-pack contract: provider families are advisory/fixture-first until validated. Each pack should add docs, policies, classes, provider helper, fixtures, JSON contracts, explainability, and tests. Do not claim first-tier or compliance parity unless platform parity tests and primary-source validation support it.

Edge cloud landmine: edge locality is not legal residency. CDN/edge cache, logs, telemetry, KV/object state, egress routing, and provider control-plane metadata may cross jurisdictions unless policy and provider evidence prove otherwise.

Bob10 next task implemented as 0.18.39_BOB10_cloud_provisioning_dry_run_lifecycle: connect cloud_provision plans to cloud_infra dry-run helper rails and emit cloud_resource registry handoff previews. Preserve dry-run-only behaviour, no live cloud API calls, no credentials, no provisioning/destruction, and no queue dispatch refactor.

Lifecycle dry-run integration must not be interpreted as permission for live cloud provisioning. cloud_provision lifecycle-plan may call cloud_infra plan actions only; live apply remains absent and provider credentials alone must never be sufficient.
